\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Logspace --- Path Hard Walk: Results}

\begin{lemma}[No edge to vertices below two]
\lean{Complexity.PathHard.not_edge_zero}
\label{Complexity.PathHard.not_edge_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PathHard.Edge}
\difficulty{4}
For every finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean tape symbols, bit
string $x$, and nonnegative integers $s,u,v$ with $v<2$, there is no edge from vertex
$0$ to vertex $v$ for input $x$ and radius $s$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Edges from the Initial Vertex]
\lean{Complexity.PathHard.edge_zero_iff}
\label{Complexity.PathHard.edge_zero_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.initLang, Complexity.PathHard.Edge, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over bits, let $x$ be a bit string,
and let $s,v$ be natural numbers. There is an edge from vertex $0$ to vertex $v+2$ at
radius $s$ exactly when the encoding of $x$, configuration code $v$, and radius $s$
belongs to the machine's initial-configuration language.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Halting with a prescribed Boolean answer]
\lean{Complexity.PathHard.ans_dec}
\label{Complexity.PathHard.ans_dec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.PathHard.A, Complexity.PathHard.St, Complexity.PathHard.St.Bd, Complexity.PathHard.St.toV, Complexity.PathHard.ans_halt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean, let $y$ be a Boolean word, and
let $o$ assign a Boolean answer to each of five oracle indices and each Boolean word.
Let $st$ be a configuration of fifteen natural-number registers, each at most $B$, and
let $q,p$ be Booleans with $q=p$. Starting with input $y$, register vector given by
$st$, the answer state labeled true if and only if $q$ is true, and no recorded result,
the abstract machine $A(a,b,f,m)$ halts with result $p$; at every earlier time its
configuration satisfies the guard requiring its prescribed precondition and all register
values to be at most $B$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Halting of the matrix computation]
\lean{Complexity.PathHard.matrix_halt}
\label{Complexity.PathHard.matrix_halt}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt.ret, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.halt, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.PathHard.A, Complexity.PathHard.Edge, Complexity.PathHard.St, Complexity.PathHard.St.Bd, Complexity.PathHard.St.toV, Complexity.PathHard.cpDst, Complexity.PathHard.cpNext, Complexity.PathHard.cpSrc, Complexity.PathHard.cp_run, Complexity.PathHard.dispatch_halt, Complexity.PathHard.gb_of, Complexity.PathHard.hv_run, Complexity.PathHard.orc, Complexity.PathHard.sbExit, Complexity.PathHard.sbReg, Complexity.PathHard.sb_run, Complexity.PathHard.shExit, Complexity.PathHard.shReg, Complexity.PathHard.sh_run, Complexity.PathHard.stepH_of, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{6}
Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean mode, let $N$ be a finite
nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let $x$ and $\beta$ be
finite Boolean strings. Suppose a fifteen-register state $st$ has every register at most
$B$, and its registers $u,t,c,z$ are zero. On input the pairing of $x$ and $\beta$, the
register program starting in its matrix-computation instruction with register values
$st$ halts while satisfying the program guard at every time before halting. Its answer
is true when $m$ is true; otherwise it is true exactly when there is an edge for input
$x$ and radius $s$ from vertex $\lfloor i/(2\cdot 2^e)\rfloor$ to vertex $\lfloor
(i/2)\bmod 2^e\rfloor$, where $s,i,e$ are the corresponding registers of $st$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Boolean word encoding]
\lean{Complexity.PathHard.wAns}
\label{Complexity.PathHard.wAns}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PathHard.Edge}
For a Boolean mode, natural numbers $s,E,i$, a finite nondeterministic Turing machine
$N$ over the Boolean alphabet, and Boolean words $x,\beta$, define a Boolean value as
follows. If the mode is true, the value is true exactly when $i<2(2^E)^2+2\cdot 2^E+7$.
Otherwise it is true when $i<2\cdot 2^E$, false when $i=2\cdot 2^E$, and true when
$i=2\cdot 2^E+1$. For the remaining indices, it is the edge predicate for $N,x,s$ at the
pair of indices $\left(\left\lfloor\frac{i-(2\cdot 2^E+2)}{2\cdot 2^E}\right\rfloor,\
(i-(2\cdot 2^E+2))\bmod 2^E\right)$ when $i-(2\cdot 2^E+2)<2(2^E)^2$; beyond that range
it is the corresponding entry, if present, of the five-term Boolean list $(0,1,0,1,1)$,
and false if there is no such entry.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Halting During the Walk Phase]
\lean{Complexity.PathHard.walk_halt}
\label{Complexity.PathHard.walk_halt}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.halt, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.PathHard.A, Complexity.PathHard.St, Complexity.PathHard.St.Bd, Complexity.PathHard.St.toV, Complexity.PathHard.ans_halt, Complexity.PathHard.leNo, Complexity.PathHard.leReg, Complexity.PathHard.leYes, Complexity.PathHard.le_run, Complexity.PathHard.matrix_halt, Complexity.PathHard.orc, Complexity.PathHard.sbExit, Complexity.PathHard.sbReg, Complexity.PathHard.sb_run, Complexity.PathHard.stepH_of, Complexity.PathHard.tailAns, Complexity.PathHard.tailVal, Complexity.PathHard.tail_halt, Complexity.PathHard.wAns, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{6}
Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean, let $N$ be a finite
nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input symbols, and let $x$ and $\beta$ be
Boolean strings. Suppose a state $st$ of fifteen natural-number registers has every
register at most $B$, and its registers $d,u,t,c,z,n,m$ satisfy
$st.d=st.u=st.t=st.c=st.z=0$, $st.n=2\cdot 2^{st.e}$, and $st.m=2(2^{st.e})^2$. The
register program started on the pair encoding of $x$ and $\beta$, at the comparison
instruction for the unary-block length, with registers given by $st$ and no answer yet,
halts with the following answer, and every configuration before it halts satisfies the
program’s instruction preconditions and has all registers at most $B$. If the mode is
true, the answer is true exactly when $st.i<2(2^{st.e})^2+2\cdot2^{st.e}+7$. If the mode
is false, the answer is true when $st.i<2\cdot2^{st.e}$, false when
$st.i=2\cdot2^{st.e}$, true when $st.i=2\cdot2^{st.e}+1$, and otherwise is determined by
the following rule: put $q=st.i-(2\cdot2^{st.e}+2)$; for $q<2(2^{st.e})^2$, it is the
edge predicate for source $\lfloor q/2^{st.e}\rfloor$ and target $q\bmod 2^{st.e}$,
using $N$, input $x$, and radius $st.s$; for larger $q$, it is the entry at offset
$q-2(2^{st.e})^2$ in the string $(0,1,0,1,1)$, with out-of-range entries false. The edge
predicate holds when the source is $0$ and the target encodes an initial configuration
of $N$, when the target is $1$ and the source encodes an accepting configuration, or
when both are at least $2$ and the corresponding configuration codes are related by one
nondeterministic step; these encodings use input $x$ and radius $st.s$.
\end{theorem}
